issues.location: 'Why the column-first loop falls off a cliff', paragraph introducing the tiled/padding program: 'A band of 16 columns keeps the working set for that band to about 16 lines instead of n, without reading a single byte more.'
issues.problem: Confusing quantity. A band of 16 int columns is exactly one 64-byte cache line, so processing one row of the band touches and fully consumes 1 line, not 16; the '16' seems to conflate the band width in elements with a line count. Across one full band pass (all n rows) the footprint is n lines, same as the naive version -- what changes is that each line is read once, fully, instead of being revisited n rows later, so the 'working set' that must survive a gap drops to essentially 0 lines, not 16.
issues.fixLooksLike: Reword to something like: 'A band of 16 columns is exactly one cache line, so each row's slice of the band is read in full the moment it is touched -- there is nothing left to reuse later, instead of a reuse distance of n lines.'
